name: postpartum care overview
title: A postpartum problem sorted into mood (blues, depression, psychosis, told apart by how long and how severe, with the PHQ-2 and EPDS screen and its cut-offs) or fever and bleeding after the first 24 hours (delayed postpartum hemorrhage, puerperal infection), each with presentation, assessment and treatment in order; panels on the normal return to baseline and on clots, discharge and the perineum

root.title: After the birth: the normal return to baseline, or a complication?
lines: the complication is whatever breaks the timetable: blues past 2 weeks · bright red bleeding back after 24 h · fever on 2 of the first 10 days

groups.title: MOOD: how LONG, how SEVERE, is she in touch with reality?
BLEEDING or FEVER after the first 24 hours
lines: bleeding in the first 24 h: see the POSTPARTUM HEMORRHAGE chart

head: h
Postpartum depression
10–20% · major depression within 6 months of delivery
MSIGECAPS: mood, sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor, suicidal
clue: Blues > 2 weeks, or SEVERE in the first 2
• low mood, anhedonia, guilt, sleep, energy, appetite
• severe: poor bonding, suicidal or homicidal ideas
• stress: NICU baby, stillbirth, conflict, feeding trouble
• poor support · age < 25 · single · family history
• partner violence · unwanted pregnancy · perinatal anxiety, poor sleep
inv: at ANY total → immediate mental health assessment

head: h
Postpartum psychosis
1–4 per 1000 · often with another mood disorder
h
Delayed postpartum hemorrhage
bleeding ↑ MORE than 24 h after birth
h
Puerperal infection
temperature > 38.0 °C on any 2 of the first 10 days, NOT counting the first 24 h
oral, at least 4 times a day
the COMMONEST postpartum complication · 4% of maternal deaths worldwide
clue: • uterus (endometritis), urine (catheter, atony), wound or tear
inv: • long labour or rupture of membranes, many cervical exams, internal monitoring, manual placenta removal
• strep or staph toxic shock syndrome
tx: IV clindamycin 900 mg every 8 h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg every 24–48 h
• or cephalexin 500 mg 4 times daily + metronidazole 500 mg twice daily

panels.title: Back to baseline: the normal timetable
items: uterus: cervix reforms in 1 week (50% of HSIL regress) · corpus non-pregnant size by 4 weeks · endometrium 3 weeks · placental site 6 weeks · lochia up to 56 days (rubra → serosa → alba)
urinary: diuresis day 2–5 · ureters normal by 2–8 weeks · normal voiding by 3 months · blood: volume normal by 1 week, cardiac output ↑ for 48 h, heart normal by 2 weeks
breasts: colostrum day 2 to ~4 · milk from day 3–5 · weight: −5–6 kg at birth, −2–3 kg diuresis, most back to baseline by 6 months · hypoestrogenic state
ovulation can come BEFORE the first period: lactational amenorrhea is NOT contraception · not breastfeeding: ovulation and menses at ~6–8 weeks
contraception from 6 weeks · NO estrogen before 21 days (clot risk); estrogen may ↓ milk (debated)
pelvic floor physiotherapy for EVERY patient, from 6 weeks

panels.title: Clots, sleep and going home
items: venous thromboembolism: 0.5–3 per 1000, greatest risk POSTPARTUM, 9% of maternal deaths (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis) → low-molecular-weight heparin

insomnia: night feeds, stress, night light, low estrogen · sleep hygiene first (no caffeine, alcohol, screens 1–2 h before bed) · cognitive behavioural therapy if persistent · rule out a mood disorder
stay: vaginal 1–2 days, C/S 2–3 days · early (2–6 h minimum) only with community follow-up
home before 48 h: check bleeding, bowel, bladder, baby care · RhIg + MMR given · NOT with preeclampsia, postpartum hemorrhage, fever or an unstable condition
perineum: clean, dry, sitz baths, peri bottle · infected tear opens, heals by secondary intention · constipation: fibre, fluids, laxatives · NO rectal medicines after a 3rd or 4th degree tear
